### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aa1b22af51a839a03af5ea61b299f399344cf9f1` — the merge of head `b25d1856f6ae3991bd5867f5e73062efbfe30e72` into base `f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aa1b22af51a839a03af5ea61b299f399344cf9f1 && git checkout aa1b22af51a839a03af5ea61b299f399344cf9f1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb b25d1856f6ae3991bd5867f5e73062efbfe30e72 && git checkout -B drift-repro f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb && git merge --no-ff b25d1856f6ae3991bd5867f5e73062efbfe30e72

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f3b428335bb9e1efdf6896afdc9cb8c60179c2fb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

94/94 at-tier stamps (control: an `os-dev` round in this same session reads 131/131 `claude-opus-5`)
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b25d1856f6ae3991bd5867f5e73062efbfe30e72`

### ① Derived judgments

Diff face against merge-base `588475c30f`: 3 files, +342/-0 — the changeset, the rule source (+99, one module-private helper `contributedNavItemsByApp` and one fold line in `buildUniverse`), the rule's test file (+216, nine cases). No deletion, no other file, `authoring-rules.ts` and `index.ts` untouched.

ACCEPT SET — `translation-target-unknown`, population of `apps.APP.navigation.ID` locale keys. Accepted now, refused before (each verified by a probe at head and by ablation to red without the fold line):
- A1. ID is the `id` of an item in a `navigationContributions[]` entry whose `app` equals APP, carried on `packages[i].manifest` (the ADR-0130 artifact entry). Verdict: correct — every `packages[]` body reaches `engine.registerApp` (plugin.ts register loop) and engine.ts 5561-5565 registers every entry unconditionally.
- A2. Same entry carried on the stack's top-level `manifest` (single defineStack; the shape `os validate` judges). Verdict: correct, same engine path.
- A3. Any descendant (`children`, any depth) of a contributed item. Verdict: correct — the fold pushes items with their subtrees intact and `translateApp` resolves nested nodes by `id`.
- A4. Regardless of the entry's `group` (resolving, missing, omitted) and `priority`. Verdict: correct — placement only.
- A5. In the per-package leg for the app-owning package, which declares no contribution of its own (resolution context = artifact `packages[]`). Verdict: correct; this is the leg where the HotCRM author met the finding.
- A6. The hint's "Declared navigation ids:" list now includes contributed ids (P2). Verdict: right behaviour; the word "Declared" is now slightly imprecise prose — non-blocking.

Still refused, verified by probes P1-P7, P12, P14, P15: an item contributed into a different app (both when that app is absent and when it is declared); an id nothing contributes, beside contributed ones, at `error` with rule id and path intact; an entry without `app` (the same drop `registerAppNavContribution` performs); empty `items`; the contribution's own `group` id (not a node in either world); an inlined `packages[]` body with no `manifest` wrapper (the shape `ArtifactPackageEntrySchema` refuses); a case-mismatched app name; and the contributor package's per-package leg still fails at the app rung, exactly as before.

Blind-spot search (the direction that matters): on the `parsed` tier this rule runs on (`authoring-rules.ts` 710-712) I found no shape that should be refused and now passes. The one divergence found is P11 — `items` authored as a record whose values carry `id` is accepted by the lint (`recordsOf`'s record branch) while the runtime would coerce non-array items to `[]`. It is unreachable through `os build` / `os validate` because `NavigationContributionSchema.items` is `z.array` and the rule reads parsed input, and it is the same pre-existing pattern `walkNav(app.navigation)` already has. Observation, not a defect.

Invariant "the fold chooses WHERE, never WHETHER" — verified against `registry.ts` 4434-4466: the early return with no contributions adds nothing; `if (!c.items.length) continue` drops nothing; the three non-empty branches each `push(...c.items)` (into the resolved group, at the root with a `nav_contribution_group_missing` diagnostic, at the root when `group` is omitted); items are pushed as authored objects, so ids and children are unchanged. Upstream of the fold the only filter is `!contribution.app` in `registerAppNavContribution`, mirrored by the lint's `if (!targetApp) continue`; `engine.ts` 5561 has no condition beyond a non-empty array; no artifact-entry flag can suppress a package. Hence the addressable-id set the runtime serves equals the union the rule now builds. What would falsify it: any future `continue`/`return` on non-empty items in `applyNavContributions` (a refusal on a missing group — option A, an id-collision dedupe, a packageId or install-state gate), a filter added in `registerAppNavContribution` beyond `!app`, a condition placed on `engine.ts` 5561, or the artifact register loop skipping a body. The three placements are pinned by the PR's tests; the upstream conditions are established by reading only, which is acceptable for this change.

PUBLIC SURFACE — none changed, measured on the shipped artifact. Built `@objectstack/lint` at head and with the rule source swapped to the merge-base blob (dependency closure identical at both refs): `dist/index.d.ts` 537 exported names both, `dist/runtime.d.ts` 11 both, `import('dist/index.js')` 349 keys both, `dist/runtime.js` 6 both, four empty diffs. `contributedNavItemsByApp` appears twice in each of the four JS bundles at head and nowhere in any declaration file; zero at base; positive control `translation-target-unknown` twice in the same four files. So the change ships (a changeset is owed) and nothing becomes importable that was not before. `check-clause2-carriers --pair 18433` exit 0, no widening tell. `Clause-②: no` holds.

Runtime honours the accepted keys — confirmed in code, not only by the card's downstream reading: `protocol.ts` 7864 and 8303 apply the fold on every served app; `rest-server.ts` 3784 and 4028 translate the served document; `translateApp` walks nested navigation by `id`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/18203-translation-target-contributed-nav.md` declares `"@objectstack/lint": patch`. Matches the diff: a bug fix removing a false-positive `error` in a released package, zero change to the exported or declared surface (measured above), no schema, no payload key. AGENTS.md 1064-1068 ties the level to the declaration — a fix takes `patch`, `Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor` — and the declaration `no` is verified, so `patch` is the consistent level. `@objectstack/lint` sits in the changeset `fixed` group with `@objectstack/cli`, so consumers move with it.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. objectExtensions rung (dev: to file) — re-derived by probe P17: a key for a field injected through `objectExtensions[]` is reported at `...objects.crm_lead.fields.sla_tier` with the identical hint a genuinely missing field gets (control 1); the rule mentions `objectExtensions` 0 times (control `navigationContributions` 4); the spec declares it and the engine registers extensions (engine.ts step 2b). Same class-(c) trap one rung down, with a wider fold surface. Agree it does not belong in this PR — escalate as its own card. Not blocking.
2. App-name rung in the contributor's per-package leg (dev: to file) — re-derived by P7: 1 finding at `...apps.crm_enterprise`, "does not define", in both worlds. Widening which app names a package may translate is a resolution-context ruling of the #16611 kind, not a rider. Not blocking for hotcrm #1907, where the owning app's packs carry the labels. Escalate as a card.
3. `check:cross-package-test-inputs` red (dev: to file, class a) — re-derived: exit 1 with `packages/spec/dist` present, naming `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` and `packages/spec/dist/`; exit 0 with the directory moved aside. Neither path is in this diff. Gate defect; own card; not this PR's.
4. "15 warnings" vs `error` (dev: noted) — confirmed: `TRANSLATION_TARGET_UNKNOWN_SEVERITY = 'error'` at line 151 on both origin/main and head; the card and dispatch understate, the PR body and changeset say `error`. Additionally `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx` 1026-1028 still states an unresolvable key is a warning — pre-existing docs drift from #16310, docs-only card, not this PR's.
5. Areas asymmetry (dev: noted) — confirmed by P10: area ids and area nav ids remain accepted and contributed ids join them; the fold merges only into top-level navigation, which does not affect membership. No action.
6. Premise refinement — verified: the rule reaches the build through `validateReferenceIntegrity` at `authoring-rules.ts` 710 although the literal rule id is absent from that file. The seat's note already corrects this.
7. Process items in the report (fifth write, model-free trailer, AGENTS.md read order, os-dev.md divergences, zero MCP calls) — process, not contract; no effect on the accept set or surface. No action from this review.
